author: naascott
text:
I have embarked on primarily focusing on the last FTR's into the highest/lowest points of price structures (ie - QM's usually). Finding the origin of an engulf of these areas are often great places to TT with very little risk. For example, many of these from the 1 minute time frame can offer many times the reward of your risk. Testing in FXT2 with about 8 pips of risk as the max has been eye-opening.

Now think about that! Risking 8 pips, you could lose 7 out of 10 trades and still make money with a reward of 15.1. Actually, you could still make money with a 90% losing streak on 10 trades where you only won one trade with this kind of RR.

author: naascott
text:
I don't think it has ever been more clearer to me than what I saw in this particular area of price on the GU. How interesting this is becoming.

The seeming logical progression 1. Price gives a clue it wants to go higher by engulfing into a CP PAZ above its flag. 2. Price engulfs out of flag indicating it wants to also go lower. 3. The second engulf point seems pivotal in that it creates a key leg that has the RBR that is used to hold price up to create the FL that is used to create the "High and Low"

of our QM. 4. Price after retesting FL, moves on to create our higher High that contains two very important FL's - the one becoming the point or origin where price will offer up the completion of the QM. 5. Once the FL is engulfed, the RBR is then used one last time to allow price to come & create the lower low of the QM.

author: naascott
text:
Some sweet PA just prior to Crude oil inventories this morning. My goal is to get so good that I can see this as it is happening. This, to me, is the real skill! Forward Sight Reading <<< we want this

1. An area of some last demand below near the top of what appears to be a cp paz, (which seem to of had a nice clear engulf).

2. Price comes off a local higher high and FTR's & stalls before dropping into it. 3. Price performs a quick engulf back up and then drops to demand. I mark that structure and look for price to hold. Sure enough it does, price then surges nicely not too long after - engulfing the FTR back up, 4. Price rises to new highs - engulfing a very nice level above - then falls back and swaps nicely with recently engulfed FTR (which is also swapping with the last FTR into the local higher high, by the way) 5. From this point some small clues are given, price RT's back and offers a HH (green rectangle). Price then RT's back and offers a HL (yellow rectangle) 6. We are now 30 minutes away from the inventories release. And it wasn't surprising to see price momo past our chop box / fake highs and into an area that held price up before reversal to new lows. (i.e. the key FL / origin of move down, MPL, or whatever you like to call it)

Lastly, it was not at all surprising to see price surge down once it got below our demand area. Thanks for reading
